PROPOSED INDICATOR AND THRESHOLD: Implement an online leading indicator using a high-sensitivity magnetic sensor to detect partial discharge (PD) anomalies in the stator winding insulation. The sensor monitors magnetic flux density variations caused by PD pulses, providing continuous health monitoring without dedicated PD sensors. A threshold is set to trigger an alert when the magnetic anomaly signal exceeds a defined limit, predicting degradation at least 6 months before a ground fault occurs.

MECHANISM: The indicator relies on the magnetic field disturbances generated by partial discharges within the stator windings. As insulation degrades, voids expand and discharge activity increases, altering the local magnetic environment. The high-sensitivity magnetic sensor captures these changes, allowing for early detection of insulation failure precursors. This mechanism operates online, identifying degradation trends before catastrophic ground faults compromise the drive train.

DEPARTURE FROM STANDARD: Standard practice relies on offline vacuum pressure impregnation (VPI) maintenance and scheduled testing. This approach differs by shifting from offline maintenance rewinding to online predictive monitoring using magnetic anomaly detection, enabling proactive intervention without waiting for scheduled outages.

LABELED PARAMETERS:
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Magnetic Sensor Sensitivity = 0.1 pT/√Hz (design choice for detecting PD-induced magnetic fields in 4.16 kV motors)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Threshold Anomaly = 1.5 × Baseline RMS (design choice to distinguish PD from normal motor operation)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Detection Horizon = 6 months (User Constraint requirement)

INDICATOR: Magnetic flux density anomaly (in nT)

THRESHOLD: 1.5 × Baseline RMS (ASSUMPTION)

VALIDATION PROTOCOL: Test at ambient temperature (25°C), duration of 1 hour per test, n = 5 independent DEVICES (motors). Data window: 10 seconds of continuous sampling per test. The detection criterion is a sustained 1.5× increase in magnetic flux density anomaly over the baseline.
